children: Guzman y Gomez's sales growth stayed solid in 1Q, but Jefferies isn't ready to join stock bulls. Guzman y Gomez said same-store sales rose by 7.1% in 1Q. This was supported by strong brand resonance and menu innovation, among other reasons. Jefferies views it as a pleasing result against a weakening consumer backdrop. "Further product innovation should help sustain momentum, although continued macro deterioration could increase the risk of consumers trading down, particularly in more discretionary dayparts," analyst Michael Simotas says. "We remain constructive on the Guzman y Gomez story, but see risk/reward as balanced given the demanding valuation." Guzman y Gomez ended last week at A$26.48. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
